chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hasan from his father who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): What do you say regarding lubrication that a person inserts while he is fasting? He wrote: There is no harm with the solid (form), so it does not contradict the first report, because the first report only permitted the use of the solid from it, and the first report addressed the liquid that reaches the cavity (stomach), and there is no contradiction between them in any state.
ai.seo_question: Does inserting a solid suppository invalidate the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *ihtiqan* (rectal insertion) during fasting by distinguishing between the physical properties of solids (*al-jamid*) and liquids (*al-ma'i*). He resolves an apparent contradiction in previous reports by explaining that the prohibition specifically targets liquids that reach the stomach, whereas solids do not carry the same ruling, thereby establishing a nuanced legal principle based on material state rather than mere entry into the body.
